name: Osteodermal Plating
description: Induces growth of osteoderms — bony plates beneath the skin — modeled on armadillo dermal armor. The plates form a flexible mosaic covering the torso, upper arms, and thighs. Each plate is approximately 2–4 cm in diameter, hexagonal, and articulated by connective tissue that allows near-normal range of motion. The plates are effective against bladed weapons and provide limited ballistic resistance — they'll stop a knife and reduce the penetration of low-velocity projectiles, but they won't stop a rifle round. The modification adds 8–15 kg of body mass and is visibly apparent — the skin over plated areas has a subtly textured, segmented appearance. Crucible Genomics offers a cosmetic overlay option that makes the plates visible through the skin as a deliberate aesthetic choice. Full plating takes a year to develop completely and continues to strengthen for up to three years.
source_organism: Dasypus novemcinctus (nine-banded armadillo), Crocodylus niloticus (Nile crocodile, enhanced density variant)
procedure: Full-body retroviral injection series with osteoblast growth stimulation, 6 sessions over 3 months
expression_time: 6–12 months for initial plating; full density at 2–3 years
reversibility: Theoretically reversible with osteoclast stimulation; practically irreversible without major surgery
side_effects: Plates may grow unevenly, requiring surgical correction
Chronic joint stress from added mass
MRI and other imaging procedures become complicated
social_perception: Signals that the user lives or works in genuinely dangerous conditions. Respected in mercenary and security circles. In civilian settings, visible plating makes people nervous — it implies the user expects to be attacked.
story_hooks: A bone-plated enforcer discovers that their plates have incorporated a foreign metallic element from their diet — someone has been lacing their food with a substance that makes the plates detectable by a specific scanner
A street clinic offers budget osteodermal plating that grows too fast and too thick, encasing the user's ribcage in a bone shell that restricts breathing
